meru-kimi-moment:
Meru walks through the 'Kimi moment,' a sequel to early-2025's 'DeepSeek moment.'
On July 17, China's Moonshot AI released Kimi K3, an open-weight model with 2.8 trillion parameters, far bigger than DeepSeek V3's 671 billion, built on total funding of only about $1.3 billion.

On standard coding, math and reasoning benchmarks it lands near top US models like Claude and GPT-5.

## Who graded the scores?

Two catches.
Those scores are mostly Moonshot's own self-reported numbers, so there's a 'teaching to the test' risk, and because it's open-weight, anyone can download the full model and run or fine-tune it themselves.

The real test comes July 27, when the full weights drop and third parties, universities, rival labs, independent researchers, can check whether the performance is genuine.

The weights did land that day.
Quartz reported that in outside evaluations right after the release, K3 sat below Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 and OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol in overall rankings but beat both companies' prior-generation models on coding and agent evaluations.

The same story carries a point cutting the other way.
White House official Michael Kratsios accused Moonshot of using banned Nvidia chips and running large-scale distillation against US models.
If that stands up, the $1.3 billion figure proves something different from what it looks like.

@@REF@@China's Moonshot AI is releasing its record-setting open-weight model for free download (Quartz, 2026-07-27)|https://qz.com/moonshot-ai-kimi-k3-open-weights-download-072726|https://qz.com/cdn-cgi/image/width=1200,quality=85,format=auto/https://assets.qz.com/media/GettyImages-2286500319-300x200.jpg

## Does this mean fewer GPUs?

If it holds up, the 'you must spend hundreds of billions on GPUs to stay at the frontier' logic that justifies hyperscaler capex, plus Nvidia's growth story and closed-model subscription pricing, all get questioned.
Fortune framed it as a possible break in the 'compute is destiny' consensus.

One thing snags on that.
Tech Times laid out what self-hosting K3 takes, at MXFP4 precision: 1.4 terabytes of fast GPU memory and 64 or more accelerators inside a single high-bandwidth interconnect domain, with native support on Nvidia Blackwell or AMD MI400.

Free weights do not mean free inference.
The wider self-hosting spreads, the more of that same class of accelerator somebody has to buy.

@@REF@@Kimi K3 Open Weights Arrive Sunday: Self-Hosting Cuts China Data Risk the API Never Can (Tech Times, 2026-07-25)|https://www.techtimes.com/articles/321551/20260725/kimi-k3-open-weights-arrive-sunday-self-hosting-cuts-china-data-risk-api-never-can.htm|https://d.techtimes.com/en/full/469840/people-visit-moonshot-ai-stand-featuring-kimi.jpg

Meru's line: a neighborhood garage tuned a car to supercar specs and wants to give away the blueprints, the road test is July 27, and if it passes, things get big.
meru-taiwan-flashpoint:
Meru pieces together a slow-building flashpoint just off Taiwan.
On May 28, Japan and the Philippines opened formal talks to draw an EEZ boundary between Japan's southernmost Ryukyu islands (Yonaguni sits 110km from Taiwan) and the northern Philippines.

## Why is Beijing furious?

Beijing is furious: it argues the water is also Taiwan's, Taiwan is China, so the deal tramples China's rights, and since early June it has pushed coast guard and government ships in as a show of force.

The pushback is not coming from Beijing alone.
Focus Taiwan reported that on June 2 Taiwan's foreign ministry asked both countries not to infringe on Taiwan's maritime rights, and that Japan's chief cabinet secretary said any deal would not legally bind 'third parties' like Taiwan.

Taipei speaking for its own share cuts against the 'Taiwan is China' premise China builds its complaint on.
The same stretch of water now draws objections for several different reasons.

@@REF@@Gov't urges Japan, Philippines to respect Taiwan's rights in EEZ talks (Focus Taiwan, 2026-06-02)|https://focustaiwan.tw/politics/202606020013|https://imgcdn.cna.com.tw/Eng/WebEngPhotos/WebOg/600/2026/20260602/1152x605_305554626751.jpg

## Did the talks come out of nowhere?

But the talks aren't a bolt from the blue.
They're one piece of a rapidly upgrading Japan-Philippines alliance: a 2024 reciprocal access pact, Japan scrapping its arms-export limits in April, Marcos's May state visit lifting ties to a strategic partnership, and Japan handing over five Abukuma-class frigates from 2027.

China sees encirclement, not fishing rights.

## What sits on Yonaguni?

The waters east of Taiwan are exactly the corridor US forces would use in a Taiwan contingency, and Japan is hardening the first island chain with missiles on Yonaguni.

That hardening is not finished.
IBTimes Singapore reported that two Chinese coast guard vessels entered Japan's EEZ around Yonaguni in late June and that China had launched a 'special maritime traffic law enforcement' operation on June 6, while the upgraded Type-03 medium-range surface-to-air missiles meant for Camp Yonaguni are slated for fiscal 2030.

Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi said that deployment would reduce the possibility of armed attacks on Japan.
The other side is moving before the shield is built.

@@REF@@Why Yonaguni Matters: China's Latest Coast Guard Move Targets Japan's Gateway to Taiwan (IBTimes Singapore, 2026-06-29)|https://www.ibtimes.sg/why-yonaguni-matters-chinas-latest-coast-guard-move-targets-japans-gateway-taiwan-88758|https://data.ibtimes.sg/en/full/91522/china-coast-guard-patrols-near-japans-yonaguni-island-claiming-jurisdiction-east-taiwan.jpg?w=1200&h=630?q=60

Meru's one-liner: since PM Takaichi called a Taiwan-Strait conflict a 'survival-threatening situation' for Japan in November 2025, China has retaliated with a travel halt, a seafood-import ban, and, the market's real nerve, rare-earth and critical-metal export controls.
Now the EEZ fight adds fresh fuel, and the odds of an armed clash tick up.

The bigger story sits under the target: Goldman lifted its 2026-2028 earnings estimates by a whopping 65%, 108% and 119%, citing much higher silicon-photonics module volumes, demand across scale-out, scale-up and scale-across networking, 1.6T/3.2T products lifting blended prices and margins, and rising AI capex. netinterest-jpm-succession: Marc Rubinstein looks at the hardest job in banking that nobody has yet been given: the one after Jamie Dimon. Dimon is 70 and has run JPMorgan for over 20 years, and in that time the bank has quietly become a machine almost too big to hand to anyone. When he arrived, total assets were about $1.2 trillion; they have since blown past $5 trillion. The annual report grew from 144 pages to 364. Headcount went from 168,847 to 320,560. The bank now sits on roughly $63.7 trillion in notional derivative contracts, $549 billion of trading and available-for-sale securities, and $29 billion of Level 3 assets, the kind so illiquid there is no market price and you have to model the value yourself. The Bank for International Settlements ranks JPMorgan as the single most complex bank on Earth. Dimon has publicly rattled off the qualities his successor will need, flexibility, analytical horsepower, people skills, cultural awareness, curiosity, resilience, and the stamina for endless travel, which reads less like a job description and more like an admission that the role has outgrown any one human. Rubinstein's point: the very scale and complexity that make JPMorgan formidable are also what make succession a genuine risk, not a formality.
potus-cpi-june: Trump takes the June inflation report and turns it into a campaign-style victory lap. His claim: consumer prices fell by the most in a single month in over six years, and the June CPI came in below the forecast of every single economist, all 67, that Bloomberg polled. He runs through the categories where prices dropped: gasoline, electricity, auto insurance, hotels and prescription drugs. Pair that with what he calls strong wage growth, and he says real wages, pay after inflation, jumped a hefty 0.8% in the month. Then he stitches it into the bigger story he likes to tell: investment pouring into the country, factory construction surging, manufacturing jobs rising and prices falling all at once, proof, in his telling, that 'the Golden Age of America is here.' Strip away the politics and there is a real market signal underneath. A CPI print that undershoots every forecaster is exactly the kind of surprise that pulls forward rate-cut bets, pressures bond yields lower and gives risk assets room to run. Whether June marks a genuine disinflation turn or just a one-month dip in noisy data is what traders will argue over, but the direction of the surprise is unambiguous.
potus-tsmc-arizona: Trump turns a corporate capex headline into a victory lap for his trade agenda. His pitch: for decades bad politicians let America's industrial base drift overseas, chasing the cheapest Asian labor to build the very products the US invented, and when he took office, leading-edge chips weren't made on American soil at all. Now, he says, TSMC, the world's largest leading-edge foundry, has announced an additional 100-billion-dollar investment in its Arizona fabs, lifting its total US commitment to a record 265 billion dollars. He frames it as proof his tariffs and trade deals are doing exactly what he promised, pulling advanced manufacturing home across autos, pharma and semiconductors alike. The post closes on the carrot behind the stick: massive hiring, massive construction, massive investment, and an open invitation, build in America and there are 'NO TARIFFS.' Strip out the politics and the market signal is concrete: the anchor of the global chip supply chain keeps pouring money into US soil, and Washington's explicit deal is that on-shore capacity buys tariff immunity. For anyone modeling where leading-edge fab capacity, and the equipment, power and construction spend around it, actually lands, Arizona just got a lot heavier.
serenity-meritz-memory:
Serenity highlights a Meritz Securities report by analyst Kim Sunwoo with a simple thesis: the market is badly misreading semis, and the DRAM shortage gets worse from here, not better.

The numbers are striking. In H2 2026, suppliers can fulfill only 75-80% of DRAM demand; by 2027, fulfillment falls into the 60% range. The market forecasts attached to the report put SK Hynix at a 3.5x 2027 P/E and Samsung at 3.9x, a deepening shortage priced at near-historic-low valuations.

Serenity adds two corroborating signals: Intel's CEO said there will be "no relief in memory supply or pricing until at least 2028," and Micron has signed 16 long-term agreements (LTAs) with major customers, many on take-or-pay terms, customers pay whether they take the chips or not. Signs that memory demand is structural, not a passing boom.
meru-china-ai:
There's a marketplace called OpenRouter that pools 400-plus AI models and lets developers pick one per job.

Its value is that it shows actual paid token usage from over ten million developers.

## Why usage, not benchmarks?

Not benchmark scores but where real money goes, which makes it the closest thing to an honest usage ranking.

The June 2026 chart has a surprise at the top.
China's DeepSeek is number one at 16.3%, ahead of Anthropic, Alibaba, Google, OpenAI and Tencent.

@@REF@@Share Of US Models Being Used On OpenRouter Has Collapsed From 70% To 30% Over The Past Year (OfficeChai, 2026-06-26)|https://officechai.com/ai/share-of-us-models-being-used-on-openrouter-has-collapsed-from-70-to-30-over-the-past-year/|http://officechai.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/1738293673355.jpeg

OfficeChai counts DeepSeek at the same 16.3%.
It reads the same chart from a different angle.
US models as a group have fallen from roughly 70% of token share a year ago to roughly 30%.

The 16.3% is one vendor at the top; this is the retreat of a whole country of vendors.
Different denominators on the same event, so the two do not conflict.

## Just Chinese users?

When people objected that Chinese users were padding the numbers, OpenRouter broke out US users only, and it's more striking, not less.

The share of tokens US users spend on Chinese models climbed from 4.5% in early 2025 to 30% in 2026, peaking near 46%.
Roughly half of America's usage is now Chinese AI.

The reason is price.
DeepSeek's cheap model costs one thirty-sixth of GPT-5.5.

@@REF@@US Companies Now Run Nearly Half Their AI Traffic on Chinese Models (Startup Fortune, 2026-07-19)|https://startupfortune.com/us-companies-now-run-nearly-half-their-ai-traffic-on-chinese-models/|https://startupfortune.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sf-16066-1784481262771.jpg

Startup Fortune reports Chinese models taking at least 30% of US enterprise token volume in a given week, peaking at 46%.
The gap shows up in list prices, with DeepSeek V4 Flash at $0.14 per million input tokens against $5.00 for GPT-5.5.
Divide 5.00 by 0.14 and you get about 36, so the ratio above is not a loose figure of speech.

Behind that sit cheaper power, labor and construction, plus an MoE design that fires only part of the brain per question, compression tricks for long documents, and 'distillation', training on the answers of top US models.

## Volume king, no revenue?

But here's the twist: heavy usage, little revenue.
Chinese models collect under 5% of the fees.

The US Congress has already opened an investigation.
thediff-overlubricated-economy:
When money flows too easily, a market can look sturdy on the surface while getting weaker underneath. That is the argument Byrne Hobart makes in this issue of The Diff, under the name an overlubricated economy.
One thing to state first. The body of this issue is for paying subscribers, so its specific figures and examples are not public. We do not invent them here. Instead we explain the concept Hobart has worked on for a while, and test it against 2026 market numbers we looked up ourselves.

## What does 'overlubricated' mean?
Too little oil and a machine grinds, but too much and it slips and spins.
Hobart sees capital markets the same way. Raising money is supposed to carry friction: due diligence, skeptical investors, the cost of capital, time.
That friction acts as a filter that screens out weak ideas. When money flows too freely and smoothly, the filter disappears, and deals that should have failed get through.

## Is that where we are now?
Said in words alone, it is just a metaphor. So we looked at the 2026 market.

@@CHK@@US IPO proceeds, H1 2026|$251B (record)|Global M&A, H1|$2.8T, +48% YoY|High-yield spread|2.77%@@IPO proceeds are a first-half record, and the risk premium demanded on junk bonds is 2.8 percent, well below the 4 to 5 percent long-run norm. Money is abundant and barely pricing risk. That fits the overlubricated condition Hobart describes.@@Checked 2026-07-23 · Renaissance Capital · LSEG · FRED (BAMLH0A0HYM2)

M&A deal count actually fell 9 percent, yet the dollar value is a record. That means a few giant deals are pulling the market, another picture that cheap money paints.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/3/3e/NYSE127.jpg/500px-NYSE127.jpg|The New York Stock Exchange. A hot IPO market is a gauge of how easily money is flowing.|Ryan Lawler · Public domain|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NYSE127.jpg

## So why is this a warning?
This is where the surface and the substance split.

@@CMP@@The common reading|Hot IPOs and a merger wave signal a confident, strong market.|Hobart's reading|Frictionless money quietly lowers the bar for what gets funded.

An overlubricated economy looks healthy from outside: deals close, indexes rise. The problem is that the standard for what gets funded is quietly falling.
That gap usually widens most right before things stop working. Which is why a stretch when everything runs smoothly is exactly when this frame is worth pulling out.

@@REF@@US IPO market hits $251 billion first-half record in 2026 (Yahoo Finance · Quartz, 2026-06-29)|https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/u-ipo-market-hits-251-144815476.html|https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/49E26484556DF243BF6530135DC68CB1DCCF196C3F792CB194A57C49F1267FF2/subgraphmysterio/resizefill_w1200_h675;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Fquartz_855%2F3573128be50d4ed3658e37ec25d11c54

@@REF@@Mega-deals propel global M&A to a record first half (Reuters, 2026-07-03)|https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/mega-deals-propel-global-m-143400389.html|https://s.yimg.com/lo/mysterio/api/B2EE22664A5BEF00EDC37BD2EFDB5F77F8AF0D5500506E353C8BB89B84E50706/subgraphmysterio/resizefill_w1200_h659;quality_80;format_webp/https:%2F%2Fmedia.zenfs.com%2Fen%2Finvestorshub_458%2Fcdb3fe6bc5c4c541c8867d7f4f3e486e
meru-leverage:
From August, Korea is putting a brake on the 2x leveraged products that let retail investors double their bet on Samsung and SK Hynix.
Meru walks through the rules, and the theme is one thing: raise the cash bar high enough to filter the small guy out.

## How much cash do you actually need

From August 5, the base deposit jumps from 10 million won to 30 million, and the minimum trade unit goes from 1 share to 20.
Brokers are also barred from the marketing trick of waiving or cutting that deposit for higher-tier clients.

The real teeth come on August 19.
Until now you could fill up to 70% of the deposit with stocks and bonds you already held, needing only a little actual cash; from that date, you need 30 million won in pure cash sitting in the account.

Holding 300 million won of bank shares won't count: if your cash is under 30 million, you can't buy more.
In plain terms, it gets much harder to average down when the price falls.

## Why not just move to Hong Kong

And this applies not just to Korean names but to overseas leverage like 2x Tesla too.
It is a signal not to just flee to the US or Hong Kong market.

The Korea Herald says the same thing.
The 30 million won cash requirement follows the buyer into single-stock leveraged products whether they are listed in Korea or overseas.

What that piece watches more closely is the other side of it.
Exchanges in the US, Hong Kong and Britain keep adding leveraged products tied to Korean stocks and indexes, and Korean investors' net buying of US stocks jumped to $2.6 billion in July from $633 million in June.
Squeeze the cash and the demand does not vanish, it moves offshore.

@@REF@@Korea's ETF clampdown may push leverage demand overseas (The Korea Herald, 2026-07-29)|https://www.koreaherald.com/article/10824501|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2026/07/29/news-p.v1.20260729.1814b2191fa94eeca8facf4fc4a358de_T1.jpg

## Will this really cut retail demand

Meru's one-liner: with the deposit hike plus the no-collateral rule, the real hurdle feels north of 50 million won.
It will cut retail demand somewhat, but whether that's enough remains to be seen.

The regulator did not wait and see.
The Investor reports that the Financial Services Commission pulled both measures, one set for August 5 and one for August 19, forward into a single date of July 31.
Proceeds from a stock sale only count toward the deposit on T+2, once settlement is done.

The same article adds that the FSC will discuss pulling forward the move to a 20-share trading unit as well, a step originally scheduled for November.
The height Meru measured stands, and only the moment you hit it has moved forward.

@@REF@@Korea moves up tighter leveraged product rules to July 31 (The Investor, 2026-07-24)|https://www.theinvestor.co.kr/article/10819533|https://wimg.heraldcorp.com/news/cms/2026/07/24/rcv.YNA.20260724.PYH2026072402110001300_T1.jpg

What slipped through is written up in that earlier Korea Herald piece.
Index-type leverage built from many names, like KOSPI 200 or Nasdaq 100, sits outside this tightening.
The examples it gives are SOXL, which chases three times the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, and KORU, which chases three times the MSCI Korea Index.
What the regulator wants to squeeze is money piled onto one single stock.

meru-adr-conv:
The same SK Hynix share costs 49% more in New York than in Seoul.
The reason is simple: the channel for converting Seoul shares into US shares (ADRs) has been shut, so nobody could sell the expensive one and buy the cheap one.

## Why was the channel shut

On July 15, Korea's securities depository confirmed it will open that channel after July 29.

The blockage ran in exactly one direction.
Bloomingbit, the Korea Economic Daily group's English outlet, reported that turning Seoul shares into ADRs means filing a separate application with your broker and clearing foreign-exchange procedures, not the instant order an MTS or HTS app gives you for overseas stocks.
Only institutions able to handle the depository steps and the FX filing used the channel, and that is why the premium set hard.

@@REF@@SK Hynix ADR premium may hold even after share conversion opens July 29 (Bloomingbit / Korea Economic Daily, 2026-07-17)|https://en.bloomingbit.io/feed/news/116450|https://media.bloomingbit.io/news/c2315797-4809-41f9-a27c-0bd208f595e0.webp

## How far can the gap close

What happens next is predictable: buy cheap in Seoul, convert, sell dear in New York.
That flow pushes Seoul up and New York down until the gap shrinks.

TSMC, which has a similar setup, trades at a steady 16-17% gap, so that's roughly the landing zone.

The same piece puts finer numbers on TSMC.
Citing Shinhan Securities analyst Noh Dong-gil, it says the premium has held at 19.1% since 2024 and averaged 17.5% through 2026.
Open the channel but leave the friction in place, and the gap does not go to zero.

## So why not overnight

There are brakes, though: only a small slice of shares can convert for now, and regulators will loosen it slowly while watching the currency.

The brakes have names.
Bloomberg reports that SK Hynix capped the Seoul-listed shares convertible into ADRs at 2.5% of shares outstanding, and that the ADR books stayed closed for issuance and cancellation until July 29 because newly issued Korean shares cannot move until they are listed on the Korea Exchange.
Opening the application window and actually moving the shares are two different things.

The premium that article measured was 33% as of Wednesday, after touching 51% at its widest.
That is a different snapshot from the 49% at the top of this card, but the direction was already set toward closing.

@@REF@@SK Hynix's 51% arbitrage trade stymied by strict conversion cap (Bloomberg via Yahoo Finance, 2026-07-23)|https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/sk-hynix-51-arbitrage-trade-073703063.html|https://s.yimg.com/cv/apiv2/cv/apiv2/social/images/yahoo-finance-default-logo.png

Meru's one-liner: good news if you hold in Seoul. Just not today.
meru-redsea:
It starts with a funeral.

Iran's supreme leader Khamenei, killed in February, was finally buried 126 days later thanks to the ceasefire, and Yemen's Houthi rebels sent a delegation.

The trouble came on the way home.
As their plane approached Sana'a airport, missiles hit the runway.

The plane was fine, but the Houthis blamed Saudi Arabia, declared their four-year truce over, and fired missiles at a Saudi airport.

@@REF@@Yemen's Houthis say Sanaa airport bombed (Middle East Eye, 2026-07-13)|https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/houthis-say-saudi-arabia-hit-sanaa-airport-declare-end-truce|https://www.middleeasteye.net/sites/default/files/images-story/Smoke%20rises%20after%20an%20airstrike%20struck%20Sanaa%20International%20Airport%20in%20Yemen%E2%80%99s%20capital%2C%20Sanaa%2C%2013%20July%202026%20%28Khaled%20Abdullah%20Reuters%29.jpg

Middle East Eye confirms the delegation was on its way back from Khamenei's funeral in Iran.
One detail cuts against the tidy version: footage showed the Iranian Mahan Air plane landing safely at Hodeidah airport, and Saudi Arabia never answered the accusation at all.
The truce was declared over before anyone had established who fired.

## So where's the oil angle?

Why does this matter for oil?
Because the world's detour route is at stake.

Since Hormuz closed, Saudi Arabia has rerouted 70% of its exports through Red Sea ports, and Korean tankers load there too.

And the Red Sea's front door, the 29km-wide Bab-el-Mandeb strait carrying 10% of seaborne crude, is exactly what the Houthis sit on.

## Did the detour close?

On 20 July the Houthis declared a naval blockade of Saudi Arabia.

@@REF@@Yemen's Houthis declare naval blockade of Saudi Arabia: What to know (Al Jazeera, 2026-07-20)|https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/7/20/yemens-houthis-declare-naval-blockade-of-saudi-arabia-what-to-know|https://www.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/10/Houthi-1727855182.jpg?resize=1920%2C1440

Al Jazeera reports that Saudi Arabia has been pushing crude west through its East-West pipeline to the Red Sea port of Yanbu, where loadings jumped from roughly 973,000 barrels a day a year earlier to about 4 million a day.
That is the 70% rerouting with a number attached.

The same piece counts Bab-el-Mandeb as carrying crude and refined products worth about 5% of total world supply in 2024.
That denominator is all supply, not the seaborne figure above.
It also runs the arithmetic on both chokepoints shut at once, roughly 25% of the world's oil and gas.

## How does Meru read it?

Meru's read: Saudi hit the runway, not the plane, as a warning.
But the Houthis, famous for fighting to the death, don't do warnings.

After Hormuz, the back door for oil could close too.
damodaran-country-risk-2026:
Damodaran's conclusion boils down to one line.
A company's risk is set by where it earns money, not where it is listed.
His annual country-risk update, the 2026 edition, is posted free and in full on his blog.

## But isn't country risk diversifiable?
The old textbook taught that country risk is something you can erase by spreading investments across the world.
Damodaran thinks that was wrong then and is more wrong now.
Markets move together in every crisis, so spreading the bet does not wash the risk out.

On top of that, a company's revenue and costs increasingly come from many countries.
So the risk attaches to the map it does business on, not to its headquarters address.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ec/World_map_blank_without_borders.svg/500px-World_map_blank_without_borders.svg.png|A world map. Damodaran's point is that a company's risk attaches to the countries it operates in, not its headquarters.|Crates · CC BY-SA 4.0|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:World_map_blank_without_borders.svg

## How does risk change the price?
Start with the term.
A discount rate is the interest-like rate used to pull future earnings back to today's value.
Earn in a riskier country and that discount rate rises.

The same expected profit is then worth less today.

The equity risk premium, or ERP, is the extra return investors demand for holding stocks instead of a safe government bond.
The higher the country risk, the larger this premium, and the more the value is cut.

## How do you measure that premium?

@@CHK@@2026 mature-market ERP|4.20%|US implied ERP (S&P 500)|4.42%|Relative-risk multiplier|1.55x@@Damodaran starts from the 4.42% ERP implied by US stock prices, strips out the default piece of US credit to reach a 4.20% mature-market floor, then for each country scales its sovereign default spread up by an equity-volatility multiplier of 1.55. The value here is the method, not the number.@@Checked 2026-07-15 · Aswath Damodaran (Musings on Markets)

So the safe mature market starts at 4.2 percent,
and the riskier the country, the more gets added on top, lifting the discount rate.

He covers about 180 countries this year.
In his data, places like India and Brazil carry premiums a few points above the US.
The exact figures sit in the table he publishes.

@@REF@@Damodaran's country risk premium data (Stern NYU)|https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~adamodar/New_Home_Page/datafile/ctryprem.html

## What if even the US isn't risk-free?
It is worth chewing on that he no longer treats even the US as fully riskless.
He rates it Aa1, not the top grade.

@@REF@@Moody's strips U.S. of top credit rating over failure to rein in debt (PBS News, 2025-05-16)|https://www.pbs.org/newshour/economy/moodys-strips-u-s-government-of-top-credit-rating-over-failure-to-rein-in-debt|https://d3i6fh83elv35t.cloudfront.net/static/2025/05/2025-05-16T215328Z_1940376832_RC28JEAAXJP8_RTRMADP_3_USA-RATINGS-MOODY-S-1024x683.jpg

He is not alone in that call.
Moody's cut the US from Aaa to Aa1 in May 2025,
projecting federal deficits widening from 6.4% of GDP in 2024 to nearly 9% by 2035.

The benchmark everyone used for "risk-free" has started to carry a price of its own.

## So what does an investor take away?
This is not a call to buy or sell any particular stock.

@@CMP@@The old textbook's reading|Country risk washes out if you diversify, so ignore it.|Damodaran's reading|Where a firm operates changes its risk, and what you should pay.

The split is over what country risk is: a cost you can diversify away, or a property that has to be priced in.

The takeaway is a durable framework.
When valuing a business exposed to emerging markets or geopolitical risk,
it turns that risk from a vague unease into a number in the discount rate that changes the price.

@@REF@@Country Risk, the 2026 edition, in full (Aswath Damodaran · Substack)|https://aswathdamodaran.substack.com/p/country-risk-determinants-measures|https://substackcdn.com/image/fetch/$s_!wC4J!,w_1200,h_675,c_fill,f_jpg,q_auto:good,fl_progressive:steep,g_auto/https%3A%2F%2Fsubstack-post-media.s3.amazonaws.com%2Fpublic%2Fimages%2F45d8df41-15aa-426e-bbc3-ec3a2e72a6f9_2262x2078.jpeg
lynalden-orange-juice-bitcoin-pe: Macro strategist Lyn Alden announced a new venture, Orange Juice, built with her team at Ego Death Capital and partners Adrian Steckel and Ruben Zweiban. The pitch, in her own framing, is 'an alternative to private equity.' Orange Juice sets out to acquire profitable small and mid-sized businesses, improve them, and then, crucially, hold them permanently, rather than flipping them on the three-to-five-year clock that defines traditional buyout funds. Sitting underneath the operating businesses is a bitcoin treasury, which is what makes the structure distinctive: cash flows from the companies and a bitcoin balance sheet are meant to reinforce each other over a long horizon. Because the announcement is short and light on figures, there is little hard data to evaluate yet, no fund size, target returns, or portfolio, and we are not filling in numbers she did not give. What is worth noting is the shape of the idea. It stitches together two threads Alden has argued for years: that permanent, cash-flow-focused ownership beats the churn of leveraged flips, and that bitcoin can serve as a long-duration treasury reserve for an operating company. Whether that combination compounds as intended is the open question, but as a design it is a clear bet against the standard private-equity playbook.
meru-battery-triple:
Datacenters are eating electricity at a frightening pace.
The IEA sees global datacenter power demand more than doubling, from 415 TWh in 2024 to 945 TWh by 2030.

Data Center Dynamics, carrying the same IEA outlook, attaches a condition to it.
Without significant investment in transmission infrastructure, up to 20% of planned datacenter projects are at risk of delay.
Demand alone does not switch a datacenter on, which is why the scramble to source power outside the grid keeps growing.

@@REF@@IEA: Data center energy consumption set to double by 2030 to 945TWh (Data Center Dynamics, 2025-04-11)|https://www.datacenterdynamics.com/en/news/iea-data-center-energy-consumption-set-to-double-by-2030-to-945twh/|https://media.datacenterdynamics.com/media/images/GettyImages-1492553626.2e16d0ba.fill-1200x630.jpg

## Why build the power next door

But America's grid is old: over 70% of its large transformers are more than 25 years old, and a new one takes about three years to arrive.

So Big Tech builds gas plants next door, or bolts giant batteries (ESS) onto solar.
ESS demand is climbing, and until now more than 90% of those batteries were Chinese.

## Why tax credits and tariffs arrive together

Washington has now moved on three fronts.
First, MACR: to earn the clean-energy tax credit you must cut the Chinese share (for ESS, below 45% in 2026, below 25% by 2030).
Second, tariffs: the rate on Chinese ESS batteries rose from 40.9% to 58.4% starting in 2026.
Third, AMPC: make the cell in America and you get $35 per kWh back.

Take the tariff apart and it splits in two.
Battery-Tech Network counts only the Section 301 duty, up from 7.5% to 25%, as aimed at batteries; the rest is a 3.4% base duty, a 10% reciprocal tariff and a 20% fentanyl levy stacked on top.
So much of Korea's new price advantage rests on the broader US-China fight rather than on battery policy, and moves with it.

@@REF@@U.S. Raises Section 301 Duties on Chinese ESS Batteries (Battery-Tech Network, 2025-09-01)|https://battery-tech.net/battery-markets-news/u-s-raises-section-301-duties-on-chinese-ess-batteries/|https://battery-tech.net/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/Battery-Tech.Net_News-Updates.png

## How wide does the price gap get

Stack the three, and the gap between tariff-inflated Chinese cells (about $87/kWh) and Korean cells built in the US ($85-90) vanishes; add the subsidy and the Korean cell drops to $50-55.

SNE Research expects the Korean share of US ESS batteries to jump to 61% in 2026 and 85% in 2027.

The catch: Korea's three makers are still in oversupply, so they must convert this window fast.

hynix:
## What an ADR actually is
Leave something with a warehouse and you get a receipt. Bring the receipt back and you get the thing.
An ADR is that receipt, for shares. It lets a Korean stock trade in the United States.
A bank holds the real shares in Seoul and issues matching receipts in New York.

Being a receipt, it should be worth what the original is worth.

SK hynix listed on Nasdaq on 10 July 2026 under the ticker SKHY.
Citibank is the depositary, and one Seoul share equals ten US receipts.
The company sold 177.9 million receipts at $149 for $26.5 billion, the largest US listing ever by a foreign company.

@@IMG@@https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/e/ea/NY_stock_exchange_traders_floor_LC-U9-10548-6.jpg/960px-NY_stock_exchange_traders_floor_LC-U9-10548-6.jpg|A US exchange floor. The same company's shares are changing hands here and in Seoul at two different prices.|Thomas J. O'Halloran · Public domain|https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:NY_stock_exchange_traders_floor_LC-U9-10548-6.jpg

## Can the receipt cost more than the thing?
It did, which is not supposed to happen.

@@CHK@@At pricing (10 Jul)|3%|14 July|51%|22 July|33%@@The gap widens and narrows but does not converge on zero. Working arbitrage would have erased a spread that size within days. That points at the plumbing, not the price.@@Checked 2026-07-27 · Korea JoongAng Daily (2026-07-15) · Bloomberg (2026-07-23)

The US receipts jumped 27% in a single session on 14 July.

## Why didn't arbitrage work?
Here is how it should run.
Sell the expensive receipt in New York, buy the cheap share in Seoul, hand that share to the bank, get a new receipt, and deliver it.
That round trip is what pins the two prices together.

The last step was blocked.
Newly issued Seoul shares cannot be transferred until they are listed on the Korea Exchange.
So Citibank kept the books for issuing and cancelling receipts closed until 29 July.

One explanation worth correcting while we are here.
People have said the cause is a Korean short selling ban. That is not right.
Short selling resumed on all listed stocks on 31 March 2025 and works normally today.
What was shut is not short selling. It is the channel between the two markets.

@@REF@@Analysts split as SK hynix's Nasdaq shares outpace its Seoul stock (Korea JoongAng Daily, 2026-07-15)|https://www.koreajoongangdaily.com/business/as-sk-hynixs-nasdaq-shares-outpace-its-seoul-stock-analysts-are-split-on-meaning/12775379|https://image.koreajoongangdaily.com/12769084.jpg?imageId=12769084&x=0&y=0&cropw=100&croph=100&panox=0&panoy=0&panow=100&panoh=100&width=1200&height=683

## Does it close after the 29th?
The channel opens, but it is narrow.
SK hynix can convert only 2.5% of its shares outstanding into US receipts,
and the $26.5 billion offering already consumed that entire allowance.
The company could have used up to 25%. It used 2.5%.

@@CMP@@The common reading|The channel opens on 29 July, so the premium goes away shortly after.|What the structure says|Only one direction really opens. With no headroom to create new receipts, US supply does not grow.

## Has this happened before?
It has. India ran the same plumbing.
Across eleven Indian ADRs the average premium was 17% over the five years from 2001 to 2005, with individual names reaching 50%.
As of July 2005, Infosys stood at 39% and State Bank of India at 28%.

The cause was identical.
Converting an ADR into shares was free, but converting shares into ADRs was allowed only up to the amount previously converted the other way.
Once that headroom filled, the premium stayed for years.

@@REF@@Premiums in the Indian ADR Market: An Analysis of Trends and Causes (NYU Stern, 2006)|https://www.stern.nyu.edu/sites/default/files/assets/documents/uat_024323.pdf

The premium is a live gauge of how much foreign money wants Korean memory.
It is also a sign that the money cannot get in through Seoul.
bilello-earnings-bubble-charts: In his free Week in Charts, Charlie Bilello poses an uncomfortable question about the market's foundation: are we in an earnings bubble? Profits are clearly booming, analysts now expect roughly 24% S&P 500 earnings growth for 2026, a sharp acceleration from +13% in 2025 and +10% in 2024. But Bilello wants investors to ask how durable that is, and he flags two soft spots. First, one-off gains. In the first quarter, just three companies, Google, Nvidia and Amazon, booked huge 'other income' from their private stakes in firms like SpaceX and Anthropic. That roughly $69 billion of other income was about 10% of the entire S&P 500's net income for the quarter; strip it out and Q1 year-over-year earnings growth would have been about 15% rather than the reported 28%. Second, the capex cycle. If corporate capital spending is at or near its peak growth rate, then the enormous earnings boost that semiconductors have delivered will start to fade, just as the hyperscalers begin absorbing the reality of depreciating AI infrastructure on their income statements. Bilello's point is not that earnings are fake, but that a chunk of the headline growth leans on investment gains and a spending cycle that may be cresting, which makes the 2026 optimism more fragile than it looks.
meru-anthropic-alibaba:
There are two kinds of AI model.

Claude and ChatGPT are restaurants: you order, they cook, but you never enter the kitchen, the recipe, the brain, stays hidden.
These are 'closed' models.

Meta's Llama and Alibaba's Qwen are chefs who publish the recipe: they release the model's brain (the weights) as a file anyone can download and run on their own server.
That's an 'open-weight' model, and download counts are its popularity score.

## How the crown changed hands

Meta's Llama was the king, until Alibaba's Qwen flooded the market with free models from laptop-size to server-grade, taking the top spot in 2025 and cementing it with a billion downloads by April 2026.

The fight is over how.

## What Anthropic asked for

In June 2026 Anthropic filed a complaint with the US Senate alleging that operators tied to Qwen ran a massive 'distillation' attack on Claude, bombarding a strong model with questions and harvesting the answers to copy its skill.

Anthropic claims 25,000 fake accounts pulled more than 28.8 million exchanges between April 22 and June 5, subscribing to Claude Code Max on stolen cards to capture even the reasoning traces.
The filing says the targets were Claude's agentic reasoning, software engineering and planning abilities.

Every demand in the letter is regulatory.
It asks for tighter export controls on advanced chips and compute, for the loophole that lets Chinese firms reach overseas datacenters to be closed, for penalties on large-scale model extraction, and for antitrust rules clear enough that labs can compare notes on distillation attacks.

There is no damages claim on that list.
The choice described in this card's closing line is visible in the document itself.

@@REF@@Anthropic Urges Congress to Crack Down on AI Distillation By Chinese Rivals (Decrypt, 2026-06-25)|https://decrypt.co/372130/anthropic-urges-congress-crack-down-ai-distillation|https://cdn.decrypt.co/resize/1024/height/512/wp-content/uploads/2026/06/decrypt-style-anthropic-dario-amodei-2-gID_7.png

## What the backdoor was

Alibaba hit back, banning internal Claude use from July 10 over an alleged tracking 'backdoor.'

Anthropic's account is that the feature was an experiment launched in March, meant to stop account abuse by unauthorised resellers and to defend against distillation.
So the thing Alibaba calls a backdoor and the thing Anthropic carried to the Senate are two ends of one episode.

Staff were told to switch to Qoder, Alibaba's own coding tool.

@@REF@@Alibaba reportedly bans employees from using Claude Code (TechCrunch, 2026-07-04)|https://techcrunch.com/2026/07/04/alibaba-reportedly-bans-employees-from-using-claude-code/|https://techcrunch.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/04/GettyImages-2269811684.jpg?w=1024

With the copyright status of model outputs still murky, Anthropic chose politics over a lawsuit.
hassabis-framework: Demis Hassabis, the DeepMind CEO who built AlphaGo, posted an essay that has racked up 11.5M views. Two claims. hormuz-meru:
The US military blockaded Iran's entire coastline, effectively an act of war under international law.

## How far does the blockade reach

The notice to mariners reported by USNI News covers far more than the strait itself.
Any ship suspected of carrying Iranian contraband is a target no matter where it sails, as far off as the Indo-Pacific, and neutral vessels bound for non-Iranian ports are still subject to visit and search.
Ships that do not comply may be met with destructive or disabling fire.

This is not one waterway closed off, it is the whole flow of goods in and out of Iran placed under guard.
The grounds for the card calling this an act of war are sitting in the paperwork itself.

@@REF@@U.S. Reinstates Naval Blockade in Strait of Hormuz (USNI News, 2026-07-13)|https://news.usni.org/2026/07/13/u-s-reinstates-naval-blockade-in-strait-of-hormuz

## Why 20% was never payable

Right after, Trump declared himself 'Guardian of the Hormuz Strait' and floated a 20% fee on all cargo passing through, then dropped it within a day.

Meru shows with simple math why the fee was never real: a supertanker carries $160M of crude, so the US fee would be $32M, versus roughly $2M in tolls to Iran.

Nobody pays a toll sixteen times more expensive than what they'd pay the enemy.

CBS News reached the same place by a different route.
It priced a single transit at $24M for a fully laden very large crude carrier and about $17M for a large gas carrier.

The International Maritime Organization said the idea would open "a very dangerous Pandora's Box," and Lloyd's List said flatly that there is no legal basis for charging vessels exercising their right of transit passage.
That is an objection to the ground the fee stands on, not to its size, which fits the card's reading that the money was never the point.

@@REF@@Trump's Strait of Hormuz fee would have cost millions, opened "a very dangerous Pandora's Box," experts say (CBS News, 2026-07-14)|https://www.cbsnews.com/news/trump-strait-of-hormuz-fee-shipping-oil-gas-costs-legality-pandoras-box/|https://assets3.cbsnewsstatic.com/hub/i/r/2026/07/14/d795061f-0a0d-47e5-9b86-b5ec13be1dff/thumbnail/1200x630/dea1e62c9f50a3cdabb9510844671367/strait-of-hormuz-ap26194339749499.jpg

## So what was the real play

So why float it?
Meru's read: it's a negotiating card.
Trump labels each strike a 'skirmish' rather than war, hits in controlled bursts, and throws out absurd demands only to withdraw them, all to push Iran back to the table.

And the oil price rising along the way isn't a bad side bet for the world's largest oil producer.
